name: Tiered model provider layer
description: One calling surface over several model vendors, so adding, dropping or switching a vendor is a configuration change and no caller has to know which vendor serves a model.
purpose: Send each planning and answering call to the vendor that serves its model name, so AI work for people keeps moving when one vendor fails or runs out of quota.
approach: Send each model call to the vendor that serves its name, and recover from transient failures and exhausted quota by retrying or stepping down a tier.
out_of_scope: Deciding which tier a piece of work needs, and writing the content of a prompt.
milestones: 1. Offline routing, tier fallback, retry and cost cases passed by the multi provider: 56 of 56, with each model name served by its own vendor. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. Live pass rate and latency per model tier recorded on the same cases, so the cheapest passing tier is known rather than assumed.
knowledge: Models route by name prefix to their vendor; a vendor with no key is simply not registered. Transient errors deserve bounded retries while quota errors deserve a lower tier, and a give-up records a process-wide outage. Price tables count input tokens only, and no live latency or pass rate per tier has been recorded. Keyless subscription-based execution through a local command-line tool is an option where no API key exists.
measures_of_success: The right provider serves each model name, a quota error falls to a working tier, transient errors are retried the right number of times, and cost estimates order tiers correctly, all on offline cases.
parameters: Model backend selection, per-tier model pins, vendor keys and base addresses, retry count and base delay, and the registry that maps tiers to model identifiers.
inputs: A planning request (prompt plus a forced tool schema) or an answering request (messages plus an optional system prompt), with a model name or tier and optional step and reasoning hints.
outputs: A raw decision dictionary for planning, answer text for answering, and a live list of available model identifiers; errors are formatted for humans.
effects: Network calls to model vendors (or a spawned local command-line process), spend, and a process-wide outage marker after a give-up.
usage_notes: Wrap vendors in the multi-provider and let the registry resolve tiers. Prefer the cheapest tier that passes the task's own evaluation, and pin a vendor only deliberately.

name: Live messaging channel transport
description: A two-way link to a live chat channel that keeps messages in order and survives malformed events and gateway failures without ending the conversation.
purpose: Receive and send messages on a live external chat channel, so each message in a conversation with a person arrives once and in order.
approach: Pass each inbound and outbound message through the channel gateway once and in order, and skip events that carry no readable message.
out_of_scope: Operating the gateway itself, and approving permissions on its behalf.
milestones: 1. Offline channel cases passed by the OpenClaw bridge: 20 of 20, covering ordered inbound messages, malformed events and dead gateways. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. Channel cases passed on a live OpenClaw gateway, once its wire shapes are confirmed against it.
knowledge: The gateway's wire shapes were written from documentation without a live gateway, so the evidence is conformance to tolerant guesses. The gateway has had a serious authentication-token vulnerability, so the bridge requires a patched version, disabled skills and plugins, and never approves permissions itself. Approvals belong to the host's decision flow.
measures_of_success: Offline cases pass: ordered inbound messages, spelling drift in keys, ignored non-message and malformed events, graceful wire failure and dead gateway, long-poll clamp, attachments, correct send arguments and ids, only allowed tools called, and idempotent close. Standing conditions: Deliver every message exactly once and in order, survive malformed events and gateway failure without raising, and restrict calls to the allowed tool set.
parameters: Token file, channel name, whether to fetch attachments, and the receive timeout in seconds.
inputs: For receive, a timeout; for send, an outbound reply with chat reference, text and optional reply-to id.
outputs: An inbound batch (messages with ids, chat references, text and attachments, a healthy flag and any error) and a send result with success and message id.
effects: Network calls to the gateway for long-poll, send and attachment fetch; close tears down the held connection. Every failure is returned as a value, never raised.
usage_notes: Run the gateway locked down as documented, call receive in a loop, treat an empty batch as normal, and add a channel through gateway configuration or a second transport implementing the protocol.

name: Overseer: risk management that raises the overall metric
description: Watches every run through cheap checks and acts only on high-risk cases; for each kind of risk it applies whatever response the metrics show addresses that risk best (a model tier, a narrow question, a rule, a hand-off), chosen per category with statistical significance, so risk is handled where it is and paid for only there.
purpose: Raises the AI's overall evaluation metric by handling each high-risk case with the response proven best for its risk.
approach: Detects high-risk cases with cheap checks and answers each risk category with the response its metric shows works best, with statistical significance against no response.
out_of_scope: Reviewing low-risk cases, which proceed untouched, and reading the full body of each operation where a compact digest is enough.
milestones: 1. Each risk category the overseer handles has a cheap detector and a labelled case set, and overseer and no_overseer have recorded results per category. 2. For each category, the selected response beats no response on that category's cases with statistical significance, at a cost the overall metric accepts. 3. The overall QAR metric is higher with the overseer on than off.
knowledge: The digest must show the evidence each label depends on, shedding old history operations first and prior escalations last so the refusal rule keeps its evidence. A failure must degrade to proceed, and a degraded flag lets a caller retry at another tier so a silent overseer is distinguishable from a healthy one. Human escalation is for genuine forks only, since routine work is AI-doable. Checked in the code on 2026-10-28: the overseer is on by default, at the quality tier in the library and at the balanced tier in the Quest host, capped per run (core/orchestrator_types.py); an older note that it is off by default is wrong. Open, for the specification owner to decide: the recommendation is to keep it as its own solution, because it watches one run from a digest, while a hint learned from past outcomes is intuition, which the owner places in the subconscious (remember-and-recall, outcome_precedents). On cheap-model routing a reviewer handed a decision scored worse than no review while the same model asked one question of fact did well, so fact_questions is the alternative to try and no_overseer is a real rival, not a floor. The other options are merging it with a learned hint into one solution, dissolving it into the working stream or the long view, or renaming it; none is decided. Unconfirmed: these two alternatives are proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's definition (2026-10-28): the overseer is responsible for risk management to improve the overall evaluation metric; it is called when cheap checks notice high-risk cases and does whatever addresses that risk category well according to metrics with statistical significance for each risk, whether a particular model tier or anything else, flexible to each type. This settles the earlier open question of keeping it. An earlier labelled run in July passed every digest on a model since replaced, but it is not in the results log; the overseer was switched on by default then.
measures_of_success: Per risk category, the chosen response beats no response with statistical significance; low-risk cases pay no review cost; the overall evaluation metric rises. Standing conditions: A failed response degrades to proceed and never blocks a run. Never decide from keywords in a model's own output.
parameters: The risk categories, each one's cheap detector and threshold, the response chosen per category (tier, question, rule or hand-off), the significance level, and the per-run cap.
inputs: A digest string built from the user message, goal, step counters, the plan, recent conversation, prior escalations and recent operation summaries.
outputs: For a flagged case: the risk category, the response applied and its signal (proceed, redirect with a hint, answer now, escalate to deep execution, escalate to a person), with a reason and a degraded flag.
effects: Cheap checks on every run; a response, possibly a model call, only on flagged cases; no other writes; never raises.
usage_notes: Selected today: the digest overseer, one prompt for every risk, after a free pre-filter. The proposal is per_risk_response.

name: Cost estimation, daily budget and host load guard
description: Stops a lane's spending at a daily token budget and pauses task pickup under host overload, without ever killing work already running.
purpose: Keeps a lane's spending and host load predictable, so a runaway day cannot drain the budget or overload the machine.
approach: Estimates what each operation will cost and holds back new work once a daily budget or host limit is reached.
out_of_scope: Real provider invoices, output-token billing, and work run on a subscription-based runner, which the daily budget does not count.
milestones: 1. Prices, cost estimates, the daily total across restarts, and the pause-and-resume guard for memory, free memory and load pass every offline case. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Shallow orchestrator calls can run away on cost, so a daily cap is opt-in and persisted. Pausing pickup is lossless because unclaimed tasks stay queued and fire on a later scan. Prices are a hand-kept snapshot of list prices, so a provider change is not noticed until the table is edited.
measures_of_success: Prices and estimates are arithmetically right, the daily total survives a restart and resets each day, bad or negative values are handled, and the guard pauses and resumes without flapping.
parameters: Provider and model names, a token count, daily limit and usage path from the environment, and optional host limits for memory percent, free memory and load.
inputs: Token counts per call, environment variables, and host samples of memory and load.
outputs: A price per million input tokens, a bootstrap cost estimate with the provider and model used, a running total with an over-limit flag and status line, and a paused or not verdict.
effects: Writes the day's tally to a usage file and signals the poller to stop picking up new tasks while over budget or overloaded; in-flight tasks are never killed.
usage_notes: Both limits are opt-in; set them per lane. Review the price table whenever a provider changes prices.

name: Evolve by metric
description: Keeps every part of QAR comparable by its metric, so a better model, method or tool replaces the current one by measurement instead of by rewrite. It also connects QAR to a tool, search engine, model vendor, agent or knowledge source through an open-source hub and the standard it speaks, so a new capability arrives by configuration and no code per integration; how far that holds is scored by score-hub-connections of the hub of hubs, over the hub registry.
purpose: Keep every part of QAR specified as a solution with alternatives, a metric and a selected implementation, so the best one is used as the state of the art moves.
approach: Select each part's implementation by its recorded measurement, and replace it when a rival measures better on the same cases.
out_of_scope: It avoids saying what QAR is for: that is the top intent, and the general machinery for checking, measuring and selecting is the evolvable-structure library's.
milestones: 1. Share of QAR solutions whose selected implementation has a recorded result on committed code and is not beaten by a rival on the same cases: 100%.
knowledge: The author's evolvable structure (intents, problems, solutions, implementations, ideals and metrics); the evolvable-structure library's checks, measurement harness and selector.
measures_of_success: Every solution has a recorded result on committed code, selections follow the measurements, and Joshua can steer by reviewing metrics without reading code. Standing conditions: Every part of QAR has a record, a current measured result and a selection that follows the measurement; a better model, method or tool replaces the current one without a rewrite.
parameters: The records under esoi, the esoi configuration, the evaluation components.
inputs: A change to the code, a new alternative, or a new model or tool to compare.
outputs: Checked records, recorded metric results and the selected implementation for each solution.
effects: Result rows are appended to the evaluation log; no model spend unless a paid arm is run by decision.
usage_notes: Run esoi check before committing and esoi run --stale after committing measured code. Paid arms follow the metric run policy.

name: Science: evidence-weighted knowledge about the world
description: Answers what a request needs to know about the world beyond the person's own material from evidence sources (a host's research and experience search interfaces first, the web after), and says for each claim where it came from and how strong its evidence is.
purpose: Gives people advice and facts about the world they can weigh, from the best evidence the host can reach.
approach: Consults the strongest available evidence source for a world question before the cheapest, and carries each claim's source and evidence strength into the working stream.
out_of_scope: The person's own material, acting in the world, and deciding which question to research next on the person's behalf.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of world questions exists, each with reference sources and the strength of their evidence, and web_with_support_check has a recorded result on it. 2. research_sources_first cites a supporting source for more claims than web_with_support_check on that set, with stated confidence that matches how often the claims hold, at a cost per answer within the chat budget.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's design: a solution for science that represents world knowledge, using existing interfaces for research and experience search, related to web search. Web research is already specified (search-the-web) and stays the open-web reader this solution calls; the library has no research-source adapter yet, so a host's research or experience search reaches a run today only as a retrieval source or a custom tool. The answer check already flags claims the turn's reads do not support and rewrites them once with their basis (core/orchestrator_judges.py).
measures_of_success: World claims cite a source that supports them; stated confidence matches how often such claims hold; a host's research sources are used when they cover the question; the chat and background work give the same answer from the same evidence. Standing conditions: Keep world knowledge apart from the person's own material. Never present general knowledge as a cited finding.
parameters: The research sources a host declares and their order, the web reader, the evidence labels, and the cost cap per answer.
inputs: A world question from the request and the host's declared research sources.
outputs: Findings, each with its source, an evidence-strength label and the passage that supports it.
effects: Calls to research sources and the web within a spending cap; no writes.
